proposed.text: Which law explicitly criminalizes the public ridicule and vilification of PWDs, and what type of provision does it insert into RA 7277?

options.text: RA 10754 — it inserts a tax penalty clause for businesses that ridicule PWD customers
RA 9442 — it inserts specific penal provisions on public ridicule and vilification into RA 7277
BP 344 — it adds anti-ridicule provisions as part of the 2024 IRR update to the Accessibility Law
RA 7277 itself — the original Magna Carta already contained anti-ridicule criminal penalties at enactment

proposed.rationale: RA 9442 (2007) inserts specific penal provisions on public ridicule and vilification into RA 7277. RA 9442, enacted in 2007 as an amendment to RA 7277, adds explicit penal provisions criminalizing public ridicule and vilification of PWDs. These provisions recognize that discrimination against PWDs extends beyond physical access barriers to include social humiliation and degrading treatment. RA 10754 (2016) focuses on financial benefits (VAT exemption, expanded discounts) and does not add anti-ridicule provisions.
proposed.explanation: This question tests which law added the anti-ridicule criminal provisions — a distinction between RA 9442 (anti-discrimination, anti-ridicule) and RA 10754 (financial benefits).
